issue.title: test_no_system_clock_display_sites fails: update gear and update panel read the process clock (sase-1bd)

task_type_fields.why_not_flake:
Confirmed true failure, not a flake: tests/test_timezone_display_guard.py::test_no_system_clock_display_sites fails deterministically on master c78eb3805 (serial, in isolation, every run). The guard is an AST scan, so the result is independent of load. The remaining violations all come from closed epic sase-1bd (update gear):

- src/sase/ace/tui/update_gear.py:80 `moment = datetime.fromtimestamp(epoch)`
- src/sase/ace/tui/update_gear.py:81 `datetime.fromtimestamp(now) if now is not None else datetime.now()` (two hits)
- src/sase/ace/tui/update_gear.py:111 `datetime.fromtimestamp(epoch).strftime("%H:%M:%S")`
- src/sase/ace/tui/update_panel_state.py:142 `datetime.fromtimestamp(failure.finished_at)`
- src/sase/ace/tui/update_panel_state.py:143 `datetime.fromtimestamp(now)`

These came from 9814d8980e (sase-1bd.1), 3786032efb (sase-1bd.3) and 21d4e12c8c (sase-1bd.4). Root cause: display and relative-age code reads the process clock and timezone instead of the configured SASE timezone. Fix: route the sites through sase.core.time. Use format_local(epoch, "%H:%M:%S") for clock text, and parse_local(...) plus local_now() for relative-age references. That is the same fix the sase-1b2 landing applied to five FINAL-deck sites in instance_card.py, overview_card.py, run_blocks.py, _agent_finalizer_receipt.py and finalizers/cli.py. Expect goldens that render the update gear's clock to shift from process-TZ (UTC in the visual fixtures) to the pinned America/New_York configured timezone; re-baseline and inspect them.
